items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-07-21
items.q: he and I got to be very, very good friends. Bernard Hebe was his name

ctx.x: And were they segregated with all the ferry boats?

Yes. Let's face it. I am born on the other side of this thing called integration. I never had too much of a problem. I was well liked by a lot of whites. My mother, at one time, worked for the Hebe family. They were one of the richest families in Greton. They owned a big barber shop, and the oldest son became a lawyer, and he and I got to be very, very good friends. Bernard Hebe was his name, his name after his father, Mr. Bernard Hebe. They were very nice people, and like I said, when my mother and father…
You said your mother worked for the Hebe's.
